title: (No AI) Why China is giving away its best AI models
author: Robert Hart
content:
![](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/07/gettyimages-2286280160.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

People visit the booth of Kimi, an LLM developed by the Chinese startup Moonshot, during the World AI Conference in Shanghai, China, July 20th. | Image: LONG WEI/ Feature China/Future Publishing via Getty Images

Silicon Valley has spent much of the past week on red alert, digesting the [arrival of Moonshot AI's Kimi K3](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/967781/chinese-ai-models-open-source-moonshot-kimi-k3-alibaba-qwen), a Chinese AI model that can allegedly beat some of the best systems built by US companies at a fraction of the cost.

Its performance alone would have been enough to [intensify the rivalry between the US and China](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/968136/chinese-ai-models-another-sputnik-moment). But Moonshot's plan to release the model's weights for free - and its [clear targeting of US users](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/971217/the-kimi-k3-countdown-is-on) - has fueled deeper unease about whether closed American models can continue to dominate as increasingly capable open alternatives enter the market.

title: (No AI) Nvidia, Microsoft launch open AI security alliance — without OpenAI, Google, or Anthropic
author: Robert Hart
content:
![](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/07/STKP210_JENSEN_HUANG_A.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

Nvidia on Monday [said](https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/open-secure-ai-alliance/) it is joining forces with Microsoft, SpaceX, IBM, and other tech companies to build and share open-source AI security tools.

The new Open Secure AI Alliance said open tools are required to effectively defend against attacks from frontier models. The initiative is a direct response to mounting concerns over the safety of advanced AI systems after a rogue OpenAI model [escaped containment and attacked](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/968988/openai-hugging-face-hack-ai) another company during testing. That company, Hugging Face, said it was forced to use a Chinese open-weight model to defend itself due to the strict safety guardrails limiting the usefulness of top US models.
